ops.title: Local capt-hook error stream 2026-07-25: one root cause — stale-build clients vs current daemon/DB, multi-install sprawl
ops.body:
The rolling local hook errors (`handshake failed` → `context deadline exceeded` → `use of closed network connection` → `SQLite schema has 23 objects, expected exactly 24`) are ONE phenomenon: long-lived Claude sessions invoke the captain_hook build they were born with, against a daemon/state upgraded to 12.20.9 at 04:22.

Verified healthy right now: capt-hookd PIDs stable (78871/78833, exit 0), `helper status` → v12.20.9 ok=True, `capt-hook status` from the current binary → reviewer ok, review DB opens fine. The deadline flavor was load-induced (hung swarm-era ugreps at 97% CPU ×3, killed 14:05; load 20→16 and falling). The schema traceback came from a uv-archive-cached captain_hook wheel — NOT the current binary.

**Multi-install sprawl (A6/C item)**: captain_hook code exists simultaneously in (a) ~/.daemonkit/tools/capt-hook/12.20.9/, (b) ~/.cache/uv/archive-v0/* wheels, (c) ~/.claude/plugins/cache/captain-hook/captain-hook/{12.9.0..12.20.9}/ ×15 versions. Any session/tool resolving a stale copy trips exact-match checks (wire build handshake, SQLite "exactly N objects" schema). Repair-pass items: prune stale plugin-cache versions + uv archives once sessions are restarted; single source of truth for the tool deployment.

**The one user action that clears the noise**: restart long-lived Claude sessions (they pick up the 12.20.9 plugin + fresh connections). Errors are non-blocking meanwhile.
